name: Brew coffee
description: A dialed-in house pour-over recipe that a grinder + scale + kettle, or a programmable brewer, can run tomorrow: 18 g of coffee to 300 ml of 93 °C water (1:16.7), about 190 s total brew time (window 3:00-3:30), with a taste-to-fix map: sour = too fast, bitter = too slow, weak or heavy = fix the water per gram.

learned_parameters.label: Coffee
learned_parameters.rationale: An 18 g dose achieves a perfect 100 sub-score (Attempt #3: 18 g -> score 100.0; Attempt #9 & #10: 18 g -> score 100.0). Deviating to 17 g caused thin and sour flow (Attempt #5: 17 g -> score 91.6, dose sub-score 71), while 19 g produced a bed packed too deep resulting in heavy bitterness (Attempt #4: 19 g -> score 91.3, dose sub-score 71). A 15.5 g dose severely underperformed (Attempt #1: 15.5 g -> score 38.1, dose sub-score 11). This aligns with SCA Golden Cup standards for a single 300 ml house mug. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 18 g. Tried 15.5 g (sub-score 11) to 19 g (sub-score 71). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 18 g and 18 g. Too high (19 g): "Heavy and bitter: the bed is packed too deep and the cup is too strong." Too low (17 g): "Thin and sour: the shallow coffee bed let the water rush straight through."

learned_parameters.label: Water
learned_parameters.rationale: A water volume of 300 ml provides an exact house serving and hits 100 on both water volume and brew ratio sub-scores (Attempt #3, #9, #10 -> score 100.0). Raising water to 330 ml or 350 ml causes cup overflow and weak taste (Attempt #6: 330 ml -> score 93.7, water sub-score 61; Attempt #2: 350 ml -> score 78.7, water sub-score 25). Dropping to 270 ml leaves the mug short of a full serving (Attempt #7: 270 ml -> score 88.7, water sub-score 61). Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 300 ml. Tried 270 ml (sub-score 61) to 350 ml (sub-score 25). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 300 ml and 320 ml. Too high (330 ml): "Brew spills past the mug: more than a house serving." Too low (270 ml): "The mug comes out short: not a full house serving."

learned_parameters.label: Brew time
learned_parameters.rationale: A contact time of 190 s yields a perfect 100 brew time sub-score (Attempt #3, #9, #10 -> score 100.0). Cutting contact time to 150 s caused severe under-extraction with sour and salty notes (Attempt #1: 150 s -> score 38.1, brew time sub-score 61). Extending time to 220 s caused minor over-extraction (Attempt #8: 220 s -> score 98.5, brew time sub-score 95). 190 s falls neatly in the standard ~3 minute extraction window for pour-over methods. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 190 s. Tried 150 s (sub-score 61) to 220 s (sub-score 95). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 190 s and 220 s.

control_effects.effect: Controls coffee bed depth and cup strength. 18 g yields 100 sub-score (Attempts #3, #9, #10). 15.5 g yielded thin/sour under-extraction (Attempt #1 score 38.1), 17 g yielded bed too shallow (Attempt #5 score 91.6, sub-score 71), and 19 g yielded heavy/bitter over-strength (Attempt #4 score 91.3, sub-score 71). Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 18 g. Tried 15.5 g (sub-score 11) to 19 g (sub-score 71). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 18 g and 18 g. Too high (19 g): "Heavy and bitter: the bed is packed too deep and the cup is too strong." Too low (17 g): "Thin and sour: the shallow coffee bed let the water rush straight through."

Controls final beverage yield and overall dilution. 300 ml achieves a full mug with sub-score 100 (Attempts #3, #9, #10). Values above 300 ml cause overflow and watery cups (Attempt #2 at 350 ml gave score 78.7; Attempt #6 at 330 ml gave score 93.7). Values below 300 ml produce a short pour (Attempt #7 at 270 ml gave score 88.7). Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 300 ml. Tried 270 ml (sub-score 61) to 350 ml (sub-score 25). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 300 ml and 320 ml. Too high (330 ml): "Brew spills past the mug: more than a house serving." Too low (270 ml): "The mug comes out short: not a full house serving."

Controls extraction level. 190 s maximizes sweetness and balance with 100 sub-score (Attempts #3, #9, #10). 150 s leaves the coffee under-extracted, sour, and salty (Attempt #1 score 38.1), while 220 s slightly over-extracts, dropping sub-score to 95 (Attempt #8 score 98.5). Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 190 s. Tried 150 s (sub-score 61) to 220 s (sub-score 95). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 190 s and 220 s.

Evaluated as 'Water per gram'. Pairing 300 ml water with 18 g coffee establishes a ~16.67:1 ratio, scoring 100 (Attempts #3, #8, #9, #10). Skewed ratios drop this term sharply (Attempt #1 at 320 ml / 15.5 g scored 21; Attempt #2 at 350 ml / 18 g scored 63; Attempt #7 at 270 ml / 18 g scored 80). Measured: Relation 'Water per gram' depends on several controls together; best sub-score 100/100.

steps: Tools: scale (dose 18 g, tare), grinder (house medium-fine), kettle (93 °C), brewer or smart brewer profile (300 ml, 1:16.7, finish 3:00-3:30).
Weigh out precisely 18 g of ground coffee (dose_g) into the brew basket to ensure the proper bed depth.
Measure and heat 300 ml of water (water_ml) to fill a standard house serving mug without overflowing or coming up short.
Initiate brewing and maintain water contact with the coffee grounds for exactly 190 s (contact_s) to extract sweetness and body without bitterness or astringency.
caveats: The 'Water per gram' sub-score is an interdependent relationship between water volume (water_ml) and coffee dose (dose_g); altering one without adjusting the other upsets the brew ratio.
A dose variation of even 1 g (17 g or 19 g) drops coffee bed sub-scores from 100 down to 71.
Increasing water beyond 300 ml causes the cup to spill past the mug and dilutes the cup, while dropping below 300 ml results in an incomplete house serving.
Contact times longer than 190 s begin over-extracting, while times near 150 s lead to sour, salty under-extraction.

problems.problem: Thin and sour: the shallow coffee bed let the water rush straight through.
problems.fix: Increase coffee dose up to 18 g to provide sufficient bed depth and resistance.

problems.problem: Too weak: watery and hollow, too much water for the coffee.
problems.fix: Rebalance brew ratio by keeping water at 300 ml and dose at 18 g (1:16.7 ratio).

problems.problem: Sour and salty: under-extracted, the water left the grounds too soon.
problems.fix: Increase contact time to 190 s so water has adequate time to extract solubles from grounds.
